files.name: CHANGELOG.md
files.body:
### Features

- **Delegate the settings to a group:** an administrator can now give the settings of Paperless Sync to a group, under *Administration settings → Administration privileges* or with `occ admin-delegation:add`, so that the person who runs Paperless needs no full administrator account of Nextcloud. The members of the group can do all that the page offers, with their own password, and nothing else of the administration. That includes pointing the archive and the inbox at the files of any user and the app at any address of the network of the server, so delegate it only to people whom you trust with those.
- **Files says what the folders of Paperless Sync do:** a note above the list in the archive and below it says that the folder is a mirror of Paperless, when it was last updated, and that changes there don't reach Paperless, with a link to Paperless. In the inbox, it says when the files go to Paperless, with a link to the failed imports, and there it says that the reason of each failure is in the `.error.txt` next to the file. People who reach a folder through a share see it too. Each person can hide each kind of the note, and *What is this folder?* brings it back.
- **Each user can also get the documents that Paperless shares with them:** set *Who gets the documents* to *Each user, those they own or may view in Paperless*, and a bill that one person of your household owns and shares with the other, directly or through a group of Paperless, reaches both of them, each with a copy of their own in their own files. When Paperless no longer lets someone view a document, their copy moves to their trash bin with the next run, and the copies of the others stay. Each copy counts against the quota of its user, and the account of the app needs the permission *View* for Groups. The connection checklist shows who also gets how many documents of whom, and a dry run lists every change with its user.
- **French and Spanish:** the settings, their messages, the connection checklist, the report of a run, the notes in Files, the Activity stream and the notifications now speak French and Spanish to accounts set to these languages, and the listing in the App Store has a summary and a description in each. A new installation on a French or Spanish Nextcloud proposes folders in its language, such as `Archives` and `Boîte de réception`, or `Archivo` and `Bandeja de entrada`. An installation in use keeps the folders that it has. The texts were drafted with the help of an AI: native speakers are welcome to correct them, and [Translate Paperless Sync](https://dennis-otto.github.io/paperless-sync/development.html#translate-paperless-sync) shows how, and how to add a language.
- **Try it in a few minutes:** `docker compose -f demo/compose.yaml up` starts Nextcloud with Paperless Sync and a Paperless-ngx with a made-up household archive on your machine alone, connects them with a dry run first and then the first run, and prints where the archive is. It makes its own password, keeps every port on `127.0.0.1`, and runs on Linux and on Docker Desktop for Windows and macOS. The README and the website show it under *Try it*.
- **The inbox keeps videos, programs and archives out of Paperless:** a video, a program or an archive in the inbox of Paperless Sync, such as after a clean-up of a computer that moved a whole folder there, no longer goes to Paperless. The file stays where it is, and the report of each run names it as *Set aside*, on the settings page, in the status and on the command line, until you move or delete it. Every other file goes to Paperless as before, however many there are, and a file that Paperless already has keeps working as it did.

### Bug fixes

- **A folder name no longer changes after the first run:** an installation that was set up with `occ` and never saved its names got new folders, and a new archive, when an administrator changed the default language of Nextcloud. A run now stores the names that it uses.
- **A failed import no longer keeps a marker such as `[P999]` in its name:** whoever may write into the inbox could upload a broken file named `Scan [P999].pdf`. In the error folder, which others may only read, Paperless Unified Search then took it for the copy of document 999 and showed them its title and excerpt. The file now moves there as `Scan.pdf`, or as `Scan (2).pdf` when that name is taken, and its `.error.txt` says what it was called. A file that an earlier version moved there keeps its name, so look through the error folder once and rename a file with such a marker.
- **The note of the trash in the connection checklist says plainly what it means:** synchronization works, and only deletions in Paperless reach the deleted folder later, after the runs set in *Required consecutive missing scans*, because Paperless shows an account in its trash only its own documents and those without an owner. Making the account of the app the owner of the documents is optional and doesn't go together with per-user ownership. Before, the note read like a fault and told you to change the owners. The notice of a dry run about an empty trash no longer orders that change either.

### Performance

- **End-to-end tests:** the two required checks of a pull request finish sooner, and each new version of Nextcloud adds far less time to them: the health checks of the containers no longer take a good part of the processors from the tests, and the two jobs share their runs by what each run costs. The result of the tests doesn't change: every scenario and every check in the browser still runs.
